what: Galaxy Digital is a financial firm built around digital assets. It trades cryptocurrency for institutions, lends against it, manages funds, advises on deals, and separately owns the Helios site in West Texas, which it is converting from bitcoin mining into leased data centre capacity for artificial-intelligence computing.
customers: Institutional investors, hedge funds, corporate treasuries and crypto-native companies on the trading and asset-management side; on the infrastructure side, large AI computing tenants leasing space and power at Helios.
money: Trading, lending and derivatives. Reported revenue is very large because it includes the gross value of assets traded rather than the margin earned.
Fees on funds and index products.
Power and data centre capacity at Helios leased to AI customers under long-term contracts.
moat: Few regulated firms can offer institutions trading, lending, custody and research for digital assets in one place, and the Helios site has something genuinely scarce: a large block of contracted electrical power with grid interconnection already approved, which takes years to obtain.
risks: Reported revenue of about $37.0B is not comparable to an ordinary company's sales; it reflects gross trading flow, so margins on it are tiny.
The trailing twelve months show a net loss of roughly $460.5M and free cash flow of about negative $2.1B.
Results swing with crypto prices, because the firm holds digital assets on its own balance sheet.
Converting Helios to AI data centres requires very large capital spending before the lease revenue arrives, and funding it means debt or share issuance.
The sixteen analysts average a $34.22 target against a $12.32 price, a gap of nearly 180% that signals extreme disagreement rather than a reliable forecast.
opportunities: Helios turns a mining site into contracted, long-dated data centre income, which markets value far more highly than mining revenue.
Institutional adoption of digital assets continues to widen, which grows the trading and custody business.
The firm holds about $2.0B of cash against $2.9B of debt.
The listing and corporate reorganisation opened the shares to a wider pool of US investors.
watch: Progress at Helios: megawatts energised and leases signed. The crypto trading business is volatile and hard to forecast; the data centre conversion is the part with contracted, predictable revenue, and its schedule decides the story.
